entities.name: main street at the scroll's end (S6's main street, continuing west)
entities.what: The town's main street running on west from the square well to the silk's cut edge: on its north side the doctor's shop 赵太丞家, the gate hall of the official's compound 官宦人家 and a low railing; on its south side the small gate roof, the hip-gable building and the 解 building, then the willows and bare trees along the bottom of the silk. In it the broad-hatted official rides out with his retinue, a porter carries shoulder-pole baskets and men walk at the well's west end. Nothing opens off it except the gate hall's passage.
entities.vis: part: north margin behind the gate scene and the shop's boards; south margin behind the south-side roofs and the bottom trees
entities.src: 余辉: 结尾三问 (问病 at 赵太丞家, 问道 at the gatehouse)
entities.note: Datum: the centre line's last point (index 3) is exactly (2000,1180), S6.road.main's first point (station -73.63). No edge is drawn as a line; the edges are where the open ground stops. edge_n: under the collectors' seal (est) to the railing's west post foot (906,883), along the railing's foot to its east end behind the seated gatekeeper (est 1060), the gate hall's front (the west block's foot v 899; est v 897 across the passage and behind the free-standing boards), 赵太丞家's front column feet (west 1488,897 measured; east est 1760), then north round the box-like structure east of the shop (its front hidden behind the bucket man, est v ~860) to the wall foot of S6's house behind the well (v 800 at the seam, S6's reading; the line at v 787-793 from u 1904 is the top of the pale mass in front of it). The well platform's west end (front edge v ~998 from u ~1903) and the free-standing boards (feet v 985-1000) stand on the street's north margin. edge_s: S6's convention (S6.road.main, edge_s at v 1300 and its open question about the south houses' hidden walls): v ~1300, where the street's painted figures stop (the retinue's feet v ~1270-1290, the porter ~1240, the bundle man 1257). The real street-side feet of the south buildings are hidden behind their own roofs and the bottom trees and lie lower: the gate roof's north posts est v ~1350, the hip-gable building's north wall est v ~1440, the 解 building's north wall est v ~1575 (its north-east eave corner (2000,1360) plus its east post's 211-px eave height). So the ground hidden behind the south roofs may add up to ~5 m to the street's depth at u 1640-2000: a question for the lead, as on S6. West of u ~1300 the open ground runs on under the bottom trees to the silk's bottom edge (v ~1770). Centre: through the traffic, about midway between the edges, easing to S6's (2000,1180). MERGE (from t1): a short ledge is drawn at the street's south edge, a double line at v ~1285-1290 from u 1043 to ~1095 (a kerb, or the lip where the ground drops to the bottom trees); edge_s takes its ends as measured points. The dashes running on east to u ~1204 are twig tips of S7.tree.bare_bottom_1117, not the ledge. MERGE: edge_n east of the shop now runs along the est front and east side of S7.str.box_shed_1855 ((1793,870), (1919,870), (1958,830)) to (2000,800), instead of (1800,860)->(1930,800), which cut through the shed's footprint.

entities.name: gate hall (门屋) of the official's compound 官宦人家
entities.what: The street gate hall of the official's compound: single storey, open to the street under a tiled roof with bracket sets (斗拱) under the eave and a lintel beam over a wide open passage between the west column, which stands on a stone block, and an east post hidden behind the man pointing the way. Inside, a lamp or hook hangs from the lintel in the east part of the passage (u ~1337), and a small dark-topped shape shows at the edge of the open door leaf (u ~1248: S7.fig.face_at_gate_door_1251, a peeking head or a small lamp, one thing); the west half of the passage holds a light door leaf standing open against the west jamb, with a ring-knocker dot, and at the back of the passage a low railed partition (the lower half of a back door, or a screen) stands under a post. West of the passage is a plain-walled west bay, where the gatekeeper sits, with a slatted panel high under its eave (a rolled bamboo blind or a lattice); a low dark-hatched panel (a door leaf folded back?) stands on the block against the west pier. No board or writing is painted on it.
entities.vis: part: west end behind the willow, east end behind 赵太丞家's free-standing tall boards, east post behind the man pointing the way
entities.src: 名画记: 官宦人家 (pin 49); 余辉: 门房指路

entities.name: main hall of the official's compound (top of the silk)
entities.what: The compound's main hall at the top of the silk: a long hip-gable (歇山) tiled roof with tile-ends along its eave and its east gable (山花, bargeboards and an ornament) showing; its west end is behind the willows. Under the eave its front is a panel between posts, covered with rows of small dark motifs, with a dark upright rectangle in its lower middle from which a thin curved outline runs out to both sides: either a patterned curtain or screen hung across the open front, gathered by a dark tie or showing a dark doorway behind it, or a patterned wall or lattice window. It is not a board of characters: the motifs are too uniform and evenly spaced. A further post stands east of the panel. No faces are painted at it.

Further post u ~1370-1377, v 240-285. entities.name: 赵太丞家, the doctor's shop (front hall)
entities.what: The doctor's shop 赵太丞家: a single-storey open-fronted shop hall facing the street under a tiled roof, with bracket sets under the eave. Between the brackets hang four lozenge-shaped tablets reading, east to west, 趙 · 太 · 丞 · 家 (趙太丞家). Below them a front beam spans from the west column to the east column, and a tall narrow board fixed to the front of the west column reads, top to bottom, 五勞七傷□□□ (the first character probably 五; the last three unclear: one with the 言 radical, perhaps 諸, one with 氵, perhaps 湯, and one with 言 or 氵). The floor is at street level. At the back stand a counter or low platform and a rack of boxes or drawers above it (t2's furniture). Its free-standing tall boards and tilted stand are t2's props.

entities.name: the 解 building (south of the street)

Under the east eave stand a table or stand and a rail, and two poles lean from the eave to the ground (t2's props). The 'corner building' S6 names is this building's north-east end, not a separate building.

Under the eave: a rail or counter top at v 1604-1630 (u 1855-1923) and a stand with legs (u 1863-1923, v 1661-1743), t2's; leaning poles (1815,1598)->(1888,1771) and (1745,1669)->(1784,1747), t2's (props that lean on the building). The tiled south part ends near v ~1700-1720; below it grass and the bottom trees' twigs, then the silk's edge (v ~1770). PLACEHOLDER footprint: the north wall's foot est v 1575 (the north-east eave corner (2000,1360) plus the post's 211-px eave height), from u ~1592 to ~1995 (the ridge's north end at 1796 is midway), its long sides along the receding direction down to the silk's bottom edge (the building runs on beyond it); builder's choice. Facing: its gable end toward the street (north). The mat awning's west end is seen at u ~1858 (v 1252-1290), above this roof's north verge. MERGE: the rail under the east eave at v 1604-1630 (u 1855-1923) is part of this building (a sill, a shelf or the top of a low wall under the eave; t2 read it as the bench's back or the building's). The things under the eave are, by ID: the stand with legs S7.prop.bench_jie_eave_1885, the two leaning poles S7.prop.leaning_poles_1888 (added in the merge) and the tub S7.prop.tub_slatted_1973. SECOND PASS: between its east post (u ~1922-1941) and the leaning board S6.prop.jie_signboard_2085, fine vertical slats show from the bar (v ~1522) down to the slatted tub's lattice band (v ~1590): either the upper part of S7.prop.tub_slatted_1973, or a slatted screen hung from the bar, which would be part of this building. See the tub's note. Also seen: the east eave's double band runs on down-left past pole A's top (1815,1598), through about (1765,1700), toward the silk's bottom edge near u ~1730; both leaning poles cross it, and their tips show above it on the tiles.

entities.name: 官宦人家, the official's compound (buildings)
entities.what: The official's compound at the scroll's end: its street gate hall with the two blocks at the gate, the railing west of it, and the halls behind it rising up the silk (the middle hall, the main hall with its patterned front, a gable behind it).
entities.src: 名画记: 官宦人家 (pin 49); 余辉: 门房指路
entities.note: The long north-south hall S7.bld.hall_ns_1620 may belong to it or to 赵太丞家; it is in neither group. The gate scene's figures (the gatekeeper, the visitor with the food box, the man pointing the way) are t1's.

entities.name: 赵太丞家, the doctor's house (buildings)
entities.what: The doctor's shop hall with its four-tablet name board and fixed front board, and the hall behind it.
entities.src: 名画记: 国医赵太丞家 (pin 48); 余辉: 太丞医铺
entities.note: The shop's free-standing tall boards (u ~1385-1445 and ~1755-1793), its tilted lattice stand, its furniture and the people inside are t2's.
